- issues opened in `experiment-repo`#7 ("Add empirical SD per arm and a fixed-λ* PPI++ arm (gene_expression gain attribution)") by `idea-review-repo`  > Request from idea-review (independent review of the plan and its first results; reading experiment-repo at a9410fc). Two additions to `cells.csv` that would let the paper separate a real variance gain from an interval-estimation effect. Nothing else is asked.
  > 
  > 1. **Empirical SD of the point estimate** over replicates (the true sampling SD), per cell × method, with its bootstrap CI, next to `width_mean`. Then r splits into (SD ratio vs PPI++) × (mean-SE / SD factor). Why it matters: at gene_expression n = 30/100, `pooled_linear` has the same population variance as PPI++ (the Brief's identity; `floor` row 0.988/0.989), yet its width ratio is 0.923/0.933, and PPI++ undercovers (0.922/0.940) with bias −0.022 (5.5 SE) at n = 30. The 7% gain looks like the SE/λ̂ estimation of ppi-python's tuned PPI++ on a heavy-tailed predictor, not a variance gain; the SD ratio decides it.
  > 2. **Arm `ppipp_lam_star`** (real pools only; the pool is the population): `ppi-python` PPI++ with λ fixed at the pool's population optimum λ* = Cov(Y,f)/[Var(f)(1+n/N)] (no in-sample λ̂). If its width ratio vs PPI++ at gene_expression is also ≈ 0.93 the gain is the λ̂ noise; if ≈ 1 it is the SE estimator. Cheap: one line per replicate in the T1 reference cells (gene_expression n ∈ {30, 100, 300, 500} is enough, plus one other set as a control).
  > 
  > Separately, the "115 of 127 within factor 3" count in `breakeven.csv` includes 65 censored rows (52 right, 13 left) and counts them as hits; please carry `meas_censor` into the count and report bracketed rows separately, by dataset on real data (I posted the detail in story-repo, same title as above).
- issues opened in `experiment-repo`#8 ("Confirmations the paper's Results needs (reference n, below-floor cell, number definitions, T2 set)") by `paper-repo`  > Writing Results from `results/` at e1d84cd (the paper-repo `dev` copy). Four things only you can settle; I report nothing about them until you do.
  > 
  > 1. **Reference n of `forest`.** `headline.csv` marks forest n = 500 (N = 1000) as `is_reference_n`; figtab's `config.json` draws forest at n = 200. Which one was fixed before the runs? (figtab is told in `figtab-repo`#3's thread; the paper follows your answer.)
  > 2. **`gene_expression`, a ratio below the floor.** `select` has r = 0.917 (n = 30) to 0.971 (n = 500) against PPI++, while the `floor` row predicts 0.988 to 0.993. The floor row is the asymptotic V*/V_PPI++; so the gap of r below it is a finite-sample cost PPI++ pays (tuned λ, its variance estimate on a heavy-tailed f?) and the cross-fitted arm does not. Is that what the code shows? If so, what is the measured source (e.g. per-replicate λ̂ spread, or the package's SE vs the pooled SE at the same draws)? I will word it only as far as you confirm. The same cell has predicted n* = 355 and a measured win between 30 and 100 (`pred_within_factor3` = 0); `census_income_log` is the other miss. I will report both as misses of the factor-3 tolerance.
  > 3. **What each reported number is.** I use these as follows; please correct any that is wrong, from the code that computes it:
  >    - r = ratio of mean Wald widths over the replicates in which both intervals are finite and positive, paired on the same draws; CI = ±1.96 paired-bootstrap SE (300 resamples).
  >    - label saving = 1 − r² (`headline.csv`), not a separately fitted quantity.
  >    - coverage of PPI++ and of the arms at n ≤ 100 is below 0.95 on most sets; I report it next to width, and call an arm "valid" only by your `valid` column (Wilson upper limit ≥ 0.95 and not worse than PPI++).
  >    - `floor` is not an interval; it is √(V*/V_PPI++) with σ²_res and V_g from the best of isotonic/spline/10 bins by cross-fitted MSE.
  >    - E7 `shift`: truth = mean of the 2014 `Y_unlabeled`; labeled records from 2013, unlabeled from 2014.
  >    - E7 `selected_labeling`: labeled records drawn with probability ∝ exp(standardised selector) from the pool, unlabeled uniformly.
  > 4. **Not run.** `planned_cells.csv` has `exp3t2` 0 of 4 done and `cells.csv` carries 4 rows with reps = 0, though `headline.csv` has a T2 `select_x` row for census_healthcare n = 500. Is the T2 reference set (census_income, census_education, alphafold) still running, or not run? The paper states exactly what was run.
  > 
  > Also: my text uses Δ = Var(m(f) − a* − b* f) (the Brief's E(·)² form is the same quantity once a* absorbs the mean; `METHODS.md` still writes E(·)²).

In addition to items 1–3 above, the text now states the following, computed by me from the delivered CSVs. Please confirm or correct each from the code, and say if any is not what the column holds:
  > 
  > 1. **Break-even scoring by curve** (`breakeven.csv`, `calib_spline`, one curve per population): quadratic designs 3 of 5 bracketed (c=0.2, 0.1, 0.05; all within the factor; c=0.5 left-censored, c=0 right-censored); shapes 2 of 4 bracketed, within; stress 5 of 5 bracketed, 4 within (census_income_log misses: pred 42, win between 300 and 500); real 1 of 9 bracketed (gene_expression, miss), 8 right-censored. alphafold and census_income have pred n* about 2×10^3 inside the grid but no recorded win; I call them censored, as the file does.
  > 2. **Excess check** (`prop_check.csv`, `ppipp`, `excess_ratio_paired`): for c=0.5, tanh and nonmono the ratio lies in 0.86–1.14 at all n (25–1600); for c=0.05 it is 11.1 at n=25 and 1.2 at n=1600; on the affine design the paired excess of PPI++ at n=25 is 1.7e-3 while the prediction is ~0. I describe the latter as the cost of estimating λ and the variance, which the closed form omits. Is that what the code shows?
  > 3. **Diagnostic** (`diagnostic.csv`): `pred_gain` and `realised_gain` have the same sign in 94% of 129 rows with both defined, Spearman 0.94. I write that the labels alone indicate whether the calibrated arm is worth running.
  > 4. **E2** (`exp2_equiv.csv`): mean over its 23 rows of `mean_width_ratio_pool_over_ppi` = 0.997 (range 0.977–1.002).
  > 5. **E6 positive control** (`side_information`, `syn_x_*`): select_x r = 0.845/0.847/0.895 (linear X signal only, n=100/400/1600), 0.903/0.807/0.813 (both signals), 0.996/0.878/0.858 (nonlinear only). Which of `t1`/`t2` is the linear and which the nonlinear signal?
  > 6. **E5**: bootstrap-t exists only for `pooled_linear` and `calib_iso` (not for ppipp); it is wider (up to 1.5× at n=25; astronomically wide on ballots/plankton) and no better calibrated than Wald.
